items.summary: Chase: Warrican won us the series Jamaica Gleaner
items.previewTitle: Chase: Warrican won us the series
items.previewSummary: SYLHET, Bangladesh (CMC): West Indies Test captain Roston Chase has credited his deputy, Jomel Warrican, as one of the main reasons behind his side’s success in the recently concluded two-match Test series against Bangladesh. The West Indies won the series 1-0 after the second Test at the Sylhet International Cricket Stadium ended in a tame draw yesterday. Left-arm spinner Warrican was named Player of the Series after finishing with 16 wickets, the most by any player across the two matches.

items.previewSummary: Sheikh Hasina has requested a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card, signalling a possible return from India. The former prime minister submitted the request through her lawyers in a letter addressed to Bangladesh's acting high commissioner in New Delhi. The communication marks her first such formal move since fleeing the country in 2024.

items.previewTitle: AI-driven analysis: McKinsey warns AI-driven analysis could slow decision-making, weaken future leadership pipeline - The Economic Times
items.previewSummary: As artificial intelligence evolves, it accelerates business analysis, posing new challenges for decision-makers. The rapid generation of insights can overwhelm leaders, creating strategic risks, as highlighted by McKinsey. Their findings stress that while analysis speeds up, human judgment remains vital for decision-making. To thrive, organizations must enhance their capacity for human oversight, ensuring a balance between AI advantages and critical executive judgment in strategic operations.

items.previewTitle: Chinese influencers stationed in Bangladesh falsely showing slums in Dhaka as India
items.previewSummary: Around 150 Chinese influencers have been stationed in Bangladesh, making content that falsely shows slums in Dhaka as neighbourhoods in India, a Bangladeshi newspaper reported. Another influencer falsely showed 'Indians drinking tea made from cow urine'.

The rapid generation of insights can overwhelm leaders, creating strategic risks, as highlighted by McKinsey. To thrive, organizations must enhance their capacity for human oversight, ensuring a balance between AI advantages and critical executive judgment in strategic operations.
